jobs.description_snippet: Technical Support Engineer | B2B SaaS **Remote, South Africa · Independent Contractor · Initial 6-month services agreement · £1,200 - £1,600 per month · Client contact: Product Lead** Keepnet isn't just scaling, we're redefining human risk and secure behaviour management in cybersecurity. Trusted by global enterprises including Vodafone, Merck, Arriva and Hershey, we reduce human cyber risk through AI-driven automation, with Agentic AI now extending that capability further. Support is where the product meets reality. Every ticket is a customer telling us something true about the platform, and every ticket is either a problem we keep answering, or a problem we solve once and remove at the source. The services cover customer issues end to end: investigate the evidence, reproduce the problem, hand a proven case to the Product Lead where a code fix is needed, keep the customer informed throughout, then help remove the underlying cause from the product, the documentation or the onboarding flow. This is a technical engagement, not a script-reading helpdesk. It involves reading logs and error records, reproducing bugs in test tenants, and coordinating with our Product Lead in a fast moving SaaS scaleup. This is a fully remote, independent contractor engagement for a provider based in South Africa. The service availability requirements are set out in the engagement terms below. **Before you apply.** This engagement requires prior customer-facing B2B SaaS support experience: a multi-tenant, cloud-based platform that customers configure and run inside their own organisation. The category matters far less than the model, and security experience is welcome rather than required. Internal IT, device support, retail and consumer call centre experience alone won't provide the platform troubleshooting background this engagement needs. Why This Engagement Matters Today, one person runs global support at Keepnet alongside their product responsibilities. That is possible because of how the operation is built: * **Discipline.** Nothing is answered from memory, and nothing closes without a cause recorded * **Documentation quality.** The help centre is maintained to the point where most questions never become tickets * **AI agents accelerate the analysis.** Evidence-based work that used to take an hour of log reading now takes minutes, so the time goes into judgement rather than retrieval * **Monitoring.** We see errors and failures in our own records, at tenant level, without waiting to be told * **Proactive support.** A significant share of issues reach the customer from us first. The conversation starts with "we noticed this on your tenant and here is what we've done", not "sorry to hear that" * **A working relationship with product.** Causes get fixed properly, so the same problem doesn't return as a different ticket next quarter As our customer base grows we need a dedicated provider for this function, so support scales with the business and senior product time go
jobs.blurb: Technical support engineer for B2B SaaS cybersecurity platform investigating customer issues and supporting product improvements for enterprise clients.

jobs.description_snippet: **This is a software development job.** You'll design, build, test, debug, deploy and maintain real systems. What's different is how the code gets written. We use agentic coding tools as a default, so a lot of implementation gets drafted by an agent working under your direction. Your time shifts toward specifying precisely, reviewing carefully, and verifying rigorously. The bottleneck moves from typing code to judging it. Day to day you'll be building [product / systems] in [stack]. Normal engineering work, at unusual throughput. We want developers, full stop. If you can't read a stack trace and reason your way to the cause, these tools won't cover for you - they'll just help you produce bugs faster. If your experience is mostly using AI tools without a developers background, this isn't the right role for you. **What you'll do** * Break work into pieces an agent can execute and you can verify * Review a high volume of generated code and catch the plausible-but-wrong * Debug systems you didn't write line by line * Build the guardrails that make speed safe: tests, types, linting, CI * Own what ships. "The agent wrote it" isn't a defence * Bring back what you learn about where the tools break **What we need** * **Real software fundamentals** - data structures, APIs, databases, and the ability to reason about correctness, performance and failure modes * **Debugging ability.** You can find the cause, not just the symptom * **Strong code review instincts.** The highest-leverage skill on this team * **Git, CI/CD and command-line comfort** * **Testing discipline** - you don't trust code you haven't verified * **Clear writing.** Vague instructions produce vague software * **Honesty about uncertainty.** "I don't understand this yet" is a feature **By level** * **Junior:** solid fundamentals and evidence you build things. Portfolio, personal projects or coursework is fine - we'll teach the workflow. * **Mid:** 3+ years shipping production code, and you've already worked this way on something real. * **Senior:** you can design systems, set standards for how the team works with agents, and mentor people through the shift. **Bonus points** * Hands-on experience with Claude Code or similar agentic tools * **Print industry experience** - prepress, PDF/PostScript workflows, colour management, variable data printing, web-to-print, or print MIS * Familiarity with MCP or tool integrations * Open-source contributions Pay: R10 000,00 - R30 000,00 per month Work Location: In person
jobs.blurb: Software developer using agentic coding tools to build real systems, focusing on code review and verification rather than implementation.
